messages:
maria: thanks for joining the all-hands — wanted to keep a short thread for follow-ups on pricing/packaging & the credits/quota questions. ask here and we'll loop in finance/product.
kevin: quick Q — do dev credits expire? i got some from the signup promo and want to know the window.
sarah: seconding that, also curious if credits apply to embeddings or just generation tokens.
amanda: good q — dev credits granted via the console currently expire after 90 days. they apply to both text generation and embeddings, but not to enterprise reserved capacity invoices. (cc @maria for confirmation)
maria: correct — 90 days for free credits. for Dedicated/Private purchases we issue invoices/credits per contract, and those are handled separately.
ryan: what's the soft limit vs hard quota behavior? e.g., if a team hits rate limits will requests queue or get 429s?
julie: from product notes: short burst requests will be queued up to the burst window, then we return 429s once queue/backpressure is exceeded. we plan to add clearer docs and a dashboard indicator for 'currently throttled' so apps can surface graceful fallbacks.
kevin: is there an escalation path for sudden traffic spikes during launches? like can we request temporary bump?
amanda: yes — for customers on paid plans we have an emergency bump process (support ticket + ops review). for self-serve customers we have automated burst allowances based on historical usage; if that's insufficient, open a ticket and we'll triage.
sarah: curious about per-API-key vs per-account quotas — we have platform teams that want global account-level budgets + per-service sub-quotas. is that supported?
maria: roadmap item — account-level quotas + sub-quota delegation is on the near-term plan (Q2 roadmap). until then, recommended pattern is create per-service API keys and manage via the Console's billing groups. we'll publish a migration guide.
ryan: any changes to per-minute / per-second rate defaults? some of our infra tests fail on staging because of changed default windows.
ajamanda: (billing-bot): FYI default limits are unchanged today: 60 requests/min for free tier, 600 req/min for standard paid. if you need a higher baseline please file the 'rate limit increase' form (link in console).
kevin: overage policy — if server suddenly uses extra tokens beyond committed reserved capacity, do we auto-bill at on-demand rates or throttle to zero?
amanda: reserved capacity customers are prioritized; excess usage is billed at on-demand rates by default but customers can opt-in to a strict cap to prevent overages. that opt-in blocks requests once the commit is reached.
sarah: will there be a clearer matrix for what features (streaming, function-calling, embeddings) are included per pricing band? a table would help.
maria: yes — product will publish an updated pricing matrix with features, rate limits, and examples of cost per 1M tokens for different workloads. target this week.
julie: follow-up action: i'll draft the matrix and share here for review.
maria: awesome — thanks. i'll ask finance to post the formal credit expiry policy and the rate-limit increase form link in the docs.
kevin: thanks! can we also add a short FAQ line about 'how to get a temporary bump for launches' so PMs know the path?
amanda: will do. creating a short runbook and ticket template now.
maria: great thread. if anyone has very specific billing cases DM amanda and cc me. we'll keep this thread updated with links. :thumbsup:
